name: thiings-grid
title: ThiingsGrid
description: An infinite, pannable grid with momentum: drag, scroll or use the arrow keys in any direction and cells render on demand from a render function.
label: ThiingsGrid
author: Charlie Clark <https://github.com/charlieclark>

props.name: gridSize
props.description: Width and height of one cell in pixels.

props.name: renderItem
props.type: (config: { gridIndex: number; position: { x: number; y: number }; isMoving: boolean }) => React.ReactNode
props.description: Renders one cell. gridIndex spirals out from 0 at the center; position is the cell's grid coordinate; isMoving is true while the grid is being dragged or gliding.

props.name: initialPosition
props.description: Starting pan offset in pixels; Home returns here.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the viewport region.

props.name: description
props.description: Screen-reader instructions linked with aria-describedby. The default explains drag, scroll and the keys.

props.name: keyboardStep
props.description: Pixels one arrow key press pans.

a11y: The viewport is a focusable region (tabIndex 0) with an accessible name (label) and the role description "pannable grid"; a visually hidden description, linked with aria-describedby, explains the controls.
Arrow keys pan by one cell, Page Up and Page Down by one screen (with Shift: sideways), Home returns to the start; keys with Ctrl, Alt or Meta pass through.
Focus is visible: a two-pixel inset outline in the ring token on keyboard focus only.
Reduced motion: when prefers-reduced-motion is reduce, releasing a drag stops where the pointer let go instead of gliding with momentum.

Right-to-left: panning is physical and does not mirror (dragging moves content with the pointer, ArrowRight reveals what is to the right), and cells are placed from a physical origin so the layout is identical in RTL.
Cells are rendered by your renderItem; make interactive cells real buttons or links with their own names. Cells are virtualized, so off-screen cells are not in the accessibility tree.
